root_cause.text: The free_irq() call in the mpu3050 driver teardown was passed an incorrect handler pointer argument, using the device structure (mpu3050) instead of the trigger structure (mpu3050->trig) that was actually registered as the IRQ handler during setup.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes line 1272 from `free_irq(mpu3050->irq, mpu3050)` to `free_irq(mpu3050->irq, mpu3050->trig)`. The CVE description explicitly states "The handler for the IRQ part of this driver is mpu3050->trig but, in the teardown free_irq() is called with handler mpu3050." This mismatch between the registered handler (mpu3050->trig) and the handler passed to free_irq() (mpu3050) prevents proper IRQ cleanup and can lead to resource leaks or use-after-free conditions.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix interrupt deregistration by passing the correct device context pointer (mpu3050->trig) to free_irq() instead of the parent structure pointer.
intent_record.what: Changed the second argument of free_irq() from 'mpu3050' to 'mpu3050->trig' in the mpu3050_common_remove() function.
intent_record.how: This corrects the device identifier passed to free_irq(), ensuring the interrupt handler is properly deregistered with the correct context pointer that matches what was registered during setup. Using the wrong pointer could cause the interrupt handler to not be properly cleaned up or lead to use-after-free issues.

The mismatch between the registered handler pointer and the one passed to free_irq() causes the deregistration to fail, leaving the IRQ handler improperly cleaned up.

bic_trace_step.reason: In the mpu3050_common_remove() function (line 1298), the free_irq() call passes 'mpu3050' as the second argument: 'free_irq(mpu3050->irq, mpu3050);'. However, examining the request_threaded_irq() call in mpu3050_trigger_probe() (line 1168-1173), the IRQ handler was registered with 'mpu3050->trig' (the trigger structure) as the device pointer argument: 'request_threaded_irq(irq, mpu3050_irq_handler, mpu3050_irq_thread, irq_trig, mpu3050->trig->name, mpu3050->trig);'. The free_irq() call must use the same pointer that was passed to request_threaded_irq() to properly unregister the handler. This mismatch means the IRQ handler will not be properly freed, causing a resource leak and potential use-after-free issues.
